- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.75) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 3–5 days.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.75), model often underestimates; adjust upward by 2–5% for next 3–5 days.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 75% above recent mean), model frequently overcorrects; apply downward bias of 3–8% for 5–10 days post-spike.  
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (price drops 5%+ from recent peak within 5 days), model often fails to recognize it; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 3–7 days.  
- For 30-day forecasts, model consistently overestimates early in the horizon (first 5–7 days); apply downward adjustment of 1–4% for first 5 days.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles (e.g., +0.5, -0.5, +0.5), model tends to lag; add 1–3% lagged sentiment-weighted adjustment to forecast.
